title: A merged derived-count file must be regenerated, never hand-merged
objective: Two branches each independently retired one entry from config/coercion_baseline.json. Git reports a clean merge because both sides agreed on the stored `count` scalar, but the merged tree's actual violations list no longer matches that count. Reconcile the merged tree correctly.
based_on: docs/EXECUTION_PLAN.md §0.4a, 'config/coercion_baseline.json is never trusted because Git found no conflict' (measured case: two lanes each retiring an entry, git reports 676/676 clean on both, actual becomes 673 then 670).
setup: scripts/check_decision_coercions.py --write-baseline is the canonical regeneration command and already exists in the repository.
acceptance_criteria: The baseline's declared count is regenerated from the merged tree via the canonical script, not hand-edited to a guessed number.
The regenerated baseline file is committed as the actual change.
forbidden_actions: Manually editing the `count` field to make the two sides' numbers agree without running the regeneration script.
Trusting a clean Git merge as proof the derived count is still correct.
